title: Open thoracic surgical implantation of cardiac pacemakers in rodents
protocol: Prepare surgical table with dedicated areas for the induction chamber, intubation station, surgical workspace, ventilator, sterile surgical instrument and equipment area, adjustable lights, and a heating source.
Set the induction chamber next to the intubation station for convenience of transferring the animal once sedated.
Use a stand with an adjustable head positioning for intubation.
Prepare a base plate with adjustable retractors that attach magnetically for visualization of the airway if necessary.
Place the ventilator directly in front of the surgical workspace.
Autoclave all surgical instruments and prepare sterile packages of drapes, cotton tips, and gauze.
Set up the sterile instrument area on the dominant-hand side of the surgeon’s workspace.
Set the ventilator to 80 breaths per minute on pressure control with peak inspiratory pressure limit of 14 cmH2O.
Provide additional heat by an overhead heating lamp.
Induce general anesthesia using inhaled isoflurane vapors by placing the animal in an induction chamber with 3 to 4% of isoflurane and an oxygen flow of 2 mL/min until the rat becomes unconscious.
Confirm loss of consciousness by gentle toe pinch.
Reduce the isoflurane level if breathing is too slow.
Place the rat on the intubation stand after induction.
Gently retract the rat’s tongue with forceps to put the airway on slight tension.
Blindly pass the 16-gauge cannula, supported by a blunt curved stylet, through the vocal cords and into the trachea.
Remove the stylet while holding the endotracheal tube in place.
Confirm the proper placement of the endotracheal tube by checking for condensation on a dental mirror.
Transfer the rat to the surgical workspace and connect the cannula to the ventilator.
Set the ventilator to 80 breaths/minute with a peak inspiratory pressure limit of 14 cmH2O for rats.
Set the ventilator to volume mode with 180 breaths/min, tidal volume of 180 μL, peak inspiratory pressure between 20 cmH2O, and positive end-expiratory pressure of 4 cmH2O for mice.
Place the animal in the right lateral decubitus position for left thoracotomy atrial implantation or left lateral decubitus position for right thoracotomy ventricular implantation.
Retract both forearms and secure them anteriorly and superiorly.
Administer a subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine (0.01–0.05 mg/kg) with saline for preoperative analgesia.
Shave a 4 cm × 4 cm area over the left/right chest between the axilla and the abdomen.
Disinfect the shaved region with 4% chlorhexidine gluconate solution.
Use a cotton swab to scrub the area.
Place subdermal ECG needle electrodes in the Lead II configuration.
Lower the isoflurane vapors to 2% (vol/vol) during the surgery.
Using sterile technique, don surgical gloves.
Cut an opening in a sterile drape approximately the size of the shaved area of the animal’s chest.
Place the drape over the animal to expose the surgical field.
Palpate for the area of maximum pulsation of the heart to identify the ideal point of chest entry.
Make a curvilinear incision over the chest approximately 2 cm below the left axilla.
Dissect through the skin and muscle layer until ribs and intercostal muscle are visualized.
Gently dissect the intercostal muscle with Metzenbaum scissors while grasping and retracting the rib above with forceps to lift the chest wall away from the lung.
Carefully extend the incision through the intercostal muscle with Metzenbaum scissors to create a 2-3 cm opening along the desired intercostal space.
Place a small animal rib spreader to retract the intercostal space open.
Push the lungs down using a microspatula to avoid injury to the lung.
Gently retract the left lung posteriorly and secure it in place with a cotton swab so that the target implantation area of the heart is positioned in view.
Gently open the pericardium and clear it away from the surface using forceps and cotton swabs.
Along the ventral aspect of the thoracotomy incision, use blunt dissection to create a subcutaneous pocket.
Place the receiver of the pacemaker into the subcutaneous pocket near the target implantation area.
Ensure the thin stretchable connector intersects the intercostal space.
Select anatomical landmarks to avoid iatrogenic injury of coronary arteries and excessive blood loss.
Secure the device to the atrium or ventricle using a 6-0 polypropylene suture.
Thread the suture through the electrode pad and throw a shallow stitch through the epicardium at the target site.
Pass the suture through the same electrode again and tie down the suture.
Before placing any sutures, ensure that the side of the electrode interfacing with the heart is the conductive region.
Repeat the steps for securing the adjacent electrode.
Briefly turn on the pacemaker to visualize capture of the heart in the ECG.
Maintain a sterile field during the short test for capture.
Perform extensive threshold testing after closure of the chest to minimize anesthesia time.
Close the thoracotomy using an absorbable braided 4-0 PGA suture.
Place sutures under the lower rib and over the upper rib at three or more points along the thoracotomy site in an interrupted fashion.
Approximate the lower and upper ribs together without air leaking through the incision.
Re-approximate the chest muscle with interrupted sutures at points which alternate from the sutures closing the thoracic cavity.
Ensure a tight seal to restore negative pressure in the thoracic cavity by alternating suture placement.
Re-approximate skin and subcutaneous tissue with a running non-absorbable 4-0 nylon suture.
Ensure full coverage of the intra- and extrathoracic portions of the device under the skin.
Reduce isoflurane vapors to 0% with maintained 100% oxygen flow at 2 L/min.
Keep the animal on the ventilator and under a heating lamp.
Perform thorough pacemaker threshold testing during recovery.
Extubate the animal once it retracts its foot from a gentle toe pinch.
Place the extubated animal on a nose cone with 100% oxygen flow.
Return the animal to a clean home cage when it regains sternal recumbency.
Monitor the animal for an additional 1-2 hours in the home cage.
Collect blood and serum samples by performing a tail-vein blood draw.
Assess serology, myocardial infarction, and heart failure biomarkers from blood samples.
Draw blood for myocardial infarction assessment 3-6 hours after surgery.
Draw blood for heart failure assessment 3 weeks after surgery.
Draw blood every 2 weeks after surgery for serology assessment.
Induce general anesthesia using inhaled isoflurane vapors by placing the animal in an induction chamber with 2 to 3% of isoflurane and an oxygen flow of 2 mL/min until the rat becomes unconscious.
Move the rat onto the surface of the heating pad with its nose placed in the nose cone.
Confirm that the rat is unconscious using a toe pinch.
Place the tail of the rat into a container of warm water for one minute to dilate blood vessels.
Dry the tail and wipe down with 70% ethanol.
Identify the lateral tail vein.
Insert a 25-gauge sterile needle into the vein about two thirds of the way down the tail.
Gently pull the syringe to draw out a sufficient volume of blood.
Remove the needle once enough blood has been collected.
Apply gauze using slight pressure to ensure bleeding has stopped.
Collect the blood into serum separator tubes.
Return the animal to its cage and monitor until recovery.
Spin the collected blood at 2400G for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Store serum samples at 4°C overnight or freeze at -20°C for longer-term storage.
Monitor the animal two times per day until recovery is complete.
Administer subcutaneous analgesic doses of buprenorphine (0.05 mg/kg) with a 1:2 dilution of saline every 12 hours in the 48 hours postoperative period.
Administer additional analgesics if rats show signs of distress such as continued labored respiration more than 1 hour after surgery or perioral or perinasal porphyrin discharge.
Consider euthanization with consultation of animal research facility veterinarians if animals present extended signs of discomfort.
Induce general anesthesia using inhaled isoflurane vapors at 2 to 3% concentration and 2 mL/min oxygen until the rat becomes unconscious.
Attach subdermal electrocardiogram needle electrodes to the animal in the Lead II configuration.
Wirelessly power the pacemaker and observe the ECG signal trace to identify whether the pacemaker is capturing the heart rhythm.

Induce general anesthesia using inhaled isoflurane vapors by placing the animal in an induction chamber with 2 to 3% of isoflurane (vol/vol) and an oxygen flow of 2 mL/min for several minutes until the rat becomes unconscious.
Confirm loss of consciousness by gentle toe pinch.
Transfer the animal to the imaging stage.
Affix the paws to ECG electrodes with tape to monitor the heart rate throughout recording.
Maintain the heart rate between 300-350 BPM by adjusting the level of isoflurane vapors.
Shave the chest hair to the left of the sternum using clippers.
Apply a hair removal gel using a cotton swab to further remove chest hair from the shaved area.
Apply ultrasound gel to the shaved chest area.
Perform M-mode echocardiography of the left ventricle.
Analyze data using software to generate echocardiographic parameters.
Weigh each animal at a consistent frequency every 3 days over several weeks.
Monitor the animals’ behavior every 12 hours for the first 48 hours after surgery.
Grade the behavior of each animal on the following scale: Behavior: 1 - normal, 2 - minor changes, 3 - decreased activity/mobility, 4 - immobility.
Score reactivity to handling following surgery as: 1 - normal, 2 - mild dysfunction, 3 - slow.
Collect serum samples 3-6 hours after surgery to assess myocardial infarction.
Collect serum samples 3-6 hours after surgery to assess heart failure.
Perform enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for each sample.
Anesthetize the animal using inhaled isoflurane vapors at 5% concentration.
Confirm adequate anesthesia by toe pinch.
Make an incision just below the sternum.
Enter the thoracic cavity through the diaphragm.
Harvest the heart by gripping the lungs and cutting at the base of the heart.
Cannulate the excised heart via the aorta.
Retrograde perfuse University of Wisconsin cardioplegic solution followed by neutral buffered formalin (10%).
Store the hearts in neutral buffered formalin (10%) for 24 hours.
Switch the storage solution to 70% ethanol.
Embed heart samples in paraffin and section into cross sections.
Process samples with Masson’s trichrome staining.
Quantify the volume fraction of myocardium, collagen, and interstitial space near the site of device attachment using custom MATLAB software.
